title: This Beetle Does a Headstand to Drink 30% of Its Weight
subject: Namib beetle

scenes.text: This beetle does a headstand every night. It's how it drinks.
The Namib is one of the driest places on Earth. Rain almost never comes.
But fog drifts in from the sea. The beetle climbs a dune and faces the wind.
Fog droplets collect on its back and roll down to its mouth.
After three or four hours, one beetle gained about 30 percent of its body weight in water.
For a human, that's like drinking around 20 liters at once.

description:
A Namib desert beetle does a headstand so fog droplets run down its back into its mouth.
In one fog event, a beetle was recorded gaining about 30 percent of its body weight in water.
Would you stand on your head for a drink?
first_comment: The original measurement is from a 1976 study in Nature. Another beetle's bumpy back even inspired fog-catching nets. What odd survival trick should we cover next?
